name: check_closed
reason: C.closedErr ('I/O operation on closed file.', :51) is the first check of every C method model in source order (after the clinic conversions for read/readline/seek, before them for readlines/truncate, after the buffer export in write); the core simulation pins it against _pyio's closed checks (an always-passing check_closed breaks it after close), and bytesIOTwinsAgree_refuted ([close, read]) runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling.

name: check_exports
reason: bufferError carries the exact message (:61-62) and C.write/C.truncate/C.close test exports > 0 where :246, :696, :714 and :889 do; the core never takes a view, but bytesIOTwinsSameClassInRange_refuted ([97], getbuffer, write) runs it (C BufferError on an in-place overwrite, _pyio succeeds), bug pyio-bytesio-getbuffer-blocks-overwrite, and BytesIOGetbuffer pins the refusals of close/truncate(0)/write past the end.

name: set_shared_buf
reason: platform applies: the body is only `self->buf_shared = 1` under Py_GIL_DISABLED (:87-89) and is empty on the default build.

name: clear_shared_buf
reason: platform applies: the body is only `self->buf_shared = 0` under Py_GIL_DISABLED (:95-97) and is empty on the default build.

name: resize_unshared_buffer_lock_held
reason: Inlined in C.write as _PyBytes_ResizeKeepOnError's outcomes (Objects/bytesobject.c:3418-3472, the BadInternalCall at :3424 for the negative alloc, the 33-byte OverflowError at :3371-3375, MemoryError at memLimit) with the state kept on every failure; BytesIOWriteFailureKeeps pins that a failed write leaves contents, position and the open flag (a 3.14-style free-and-close fails it) and bytesIOTwinsSameClassNoExport_refuted runs the negative-size SystemError, bug pyio-bytesio-write-near-maxsize-systemerror; its getvalue() caller is unmodelled (see that row).

name: scan_eol_lock_held
reason: C.scanEol follows :133-152 (pos >= string_size gives 0, len clamped to maxlen when negative or too large, memchr for '\n' giving n - start + 1); the core simulation pins it through readline/readlines/next against _pyio's byte-at-a-time IOBase.readline loop (lineLen), and bytesIOReadlinesHintDoc_refuted runs it in the readlines loop, bug pyio-readlines-hint-stops-early.

name: unshare_buffer_lock_held
reason: The body (allocate `size` bytes, copy string_size bytes, replace self->buf so later writes cannot touch an escaped bytes object, :167-173) survives only as the 'Negative size passed to PyBytes_FromStringAndSize' message and the memLimit failure in C.write; with value semantics the copy is invisible, so an unshare that returned 0 without copying satisfies tell-after-write and failed-write-keeps-state, and the model docstring's claim that copy-on-write sharing is unobservable is false (gh-160181 below).

name: resize_buffer_lock_held
reason: C.write mirrors the Python-visible parts of :181-229: OverflowError 'new buffer size too large' above PY_SSIZE_T_MAX (:194-195, :225-228), the major-upsize alloc = size + 1 that turns negative at exactly PY_SSIZE_T_MAX and so reaches the SystemError (refuted, bug pyio-bytesio-write-near-maxsize-systemerror), and the allocation failure with state kept (BytesIOWriteFailureKeeps); the over-allocation policy only decides whether a below-bound request allocates, which the model's bound makes unobservable, and the shared branch hands off to ResizeKeepOnError-safe callees.

name: write_bytes_lock_held
reason: Success and failure paths are pinned (writes-concat, getvalue-zero-fill, failed-write-keeps-state, core, in-range and no-export refutations), but the argument is a plain byte list, so PyObject_GetBuffer (:242) calling a Python __buffer__ that raises, closes, takes a view, seeks or writes before the checks at :246 and the reads of pos at :256-257 is not expressible, and the in-place path under SHARED_BUF (:258-269, :286) is modelled by value only: 3.15.2 overwrites an escaped-then-dropped buffer whose hash is cached, leaving a stale hash (gh-160181, fixed on main via HASHED_BUF), which no property can see.

name: bytesio_get_closed
reason: `.closed => s.closed` with closed exactly when C clears buf (close, :890) and cleared by an __init__ with a value (:1099); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.closed in every state, so an always-False getter fails after close.

name: _io_BytesIO_readable_impl
reason: C.xstep .readable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:326-327); BytesIOInquiries pins the exact ValueError on a closed stream, True on an open one, no state change and agreement with _pyio (_pyio.py:1022-1025), so neither an always-raising nor an always-True body passes.

name: _io_BytesIO_writable_impl
reason: C.xstep .writable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:341-342); BytesIOInquiries pins both branches, no state change and agreement with _pyio.py:1027-1030.

name: _io_BytesIO_seekable_impl
reason: C.xstep .seekable is CHECK_CLOSED then True (:356-357); BytesIOInquiries pins both branches, no state change and agreement with _pyio.py:1032-1035.

name: _io_BytesIO_flush_impl
reason: C.xstep .flush is CHECK_CLOSED then None (:371-372); BytesIOInquiries pins the closed ValueError, None when open and no state change, against IOBase.flush (_pyio.py _checkClosed).

name: _io_BytesIO_getbuffer_impl
reason: The model is CHECK_CLOSED then exports + 1 and returns None: the memoryview over string_size writable bytes of the live buffer (:396-402) is not modelled (pyio-bytesio-getbuffer's own note says so), so a getbuffer that returned a detached copy and bumped the count satisfies in-range, getbuffer and release-exports; writes through the view, the main documented use (io.rst:740-749), are outside every property.

name: _io_BytesIO_getvalue_impl
reason: C.step .getvalue is CHECK_CLOSED then `bytes buf`: the copy-when-small-or-exported branch (:417-419), the unshare/resize to string_size with its NULL return (:421-430) and the zero-copy return of self->buf (:431-432) are not mirrored, so a getvalue that returned self->buf with a live view, or one that never sized it, passes zero-fill, writes-concat and core; 3.15.2 has a real defect on this path (getvalue() returns bytes with a stale cached hash after an in-place write, gh-160181).

name: _io_BytesIO_isatty_impl
reason: C.xstep .isatty is CHECK_CLOSED then False (:448-449); BytesIOInquiries pins the closed ValueError, False when open, no state change and agreement with IOBase.isatty.

name: _io_BytesIO_tell_impl
reason: C.step .tell is CHECK_CLOSED then pos (:463-464); the core simulation pins it against _pyio's tell after every operation sequence, including positions past the end.

name: read_bytes_lock_held
reason: C.readBytes returns the slice and advances pos, which covers the general and size == 0 branches (:487-493), but the zero-copy branch (:476-482: size > 1, pos == 0, whole buffer, exports == 0, return self->buf) is not mirrored, so a fast path that ignored the exports guard (letting a view mutate the returned bytes) passes core and read-after-seek; that returned object is also how a hashed internal buffer escapes in gh-160181.

name: _io_BytesIO_read_impl
reason: C.read follows the clinic optSsize conversion then :514-524 (CHECK_CLOSED, n = string_size - pos, negative or too-large size clamped to max(n, 0)); the core simulation, read-after-seek (every p, n >= 0 including p past the end), bytesIOTwinsAgree_refuted and the __index__ models (readObj, read-index-twins refuted) pin it.

name: _io_BytesIO_read1_impl
reason: The body is `return _io_BytesIO_read_impl(self, size)` (:544) and C.step maps .read1 to C.read with the same converter (clinic :278); the core simulation runs read1 in arbitrary sequences against _pyio's read1 (= read), so a read1 with other behaviour fails it.

name: _io_BytesIO_readline_impl
reason: C.readline is optSsize, CHECK_CLOSED, scan_eol(size), read_bytes (:566-570); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.readline for every size, and bytesIOTwinsSameClassNoAllocFail_refuted (readline(0) on a closed stream: C ValueError, _pyio b'') runs it, bug pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling.

name: _io_BytesIO_readlines_impl
reason: C.readlines follows :594-631: CHECK_CLOSED before the hint, PyLong_AsSsize_t for an int, -1 for None, the 'integer argument expected, got 'float'' TypeError (readlinesFloat), and a loop that breaks once maxsize > 0 and size >= maxsize; the core pins it against IOBase.readlines, and the hint-doc and float-twins refutations run it, bugs pyio-readlines-hint-stops-early and pyio-bytesio-twin-argument-handling (list allocation failures excluded by the model's allocation bound).

name: _io_BytesIO_readinto_impl
reason: C.readinto and C.readintoSelf follow :657-675 (CHECK_CLOSED, len clamped to string_size - pos, 0 without moving when pos is past the end, memmove, pos += len); the core pins readinto into a foreign bytearray against BufferedIOBase._readinto, and BytesIOReadintoOverlap pins the overlapping copy into the stream's own view for every position, offset and length.

name: _io_BytesIO_truncate_impl
reason: C.truncate and C.truncateObj follow :695-726: CHECK_CLOSED and CHECK_EXPORTS before conversion, PyLong_AsLong through __index__ (hooks that close, take a view, seek or write), the 'negative size value' ValueError, the re-checks at :713-714, then a shrink only below string_size with pos untouched; BytesIOTruncateRecheck pins the re-entrancy guard, truncate-keeps-position and truncate-result the documented semantics, core the twin agreement, and truncate-index-twins is refuted (_pyio deadlock), bug pyio-bytesio-truncate-index-deadlock.

name: bytesio_iternext_lock_held
reason: C.next is CHECK_CLOSED, scan_eol(-1), NULL without an exception (StopIteration) when 0, else read_bytes (:737-744); the core simulation pins it against IOBase.__next__ (StopIteration on an empty line) in every state.

name: bytesio_iternext
reason: The tp_iternext slot only wraps the lock-held body in a critical section (:751-753), a no-op on the default build; C.step .next is that body and the core pins it against IOBase.__next__.

name: _io_BytesIO_seek_impl
reason: C.seek mirrors :777-814 in order, and the core pins whence 0/1/2, clamping and the invalid-whence ValueError against _pyio, but no listed theorem reaches the two 'new position too large' guards (:789-793, :797-801): the core's Small hypothesis excludes them, read-after-seek is whence 0 only, and bytesIOTwinsSameClass_refuted fails in the clinic converter before the impl, so a seek that silently wrapped pos passes; a refutation running [seek(maxsize), seek(maxsize, 1)] (already in the bug's reproducer) would cover it.

name: _io_BytesIO_write_impl
reason: The body converts write_bytes_lock_held's count to an int or returns NULL (:832-833), which is C.write's `.ok (.int len)` / error; tell-after-write pins the returned count on every success and writes-concat makes successes non-vacuous, so a wrapper returning another count or always failing fails them.

name: _io_BytesIO_writelines_impl
reason: C.writelinesLoop takes a Lean list of byte strings, so PyObject_GetIter failing (:857-859), an iterator that raises (PyIter_Next then PyErr_Occurred, :861, :871-873), non-buffer items, and an iterator whose __next__ closes the stream or takes a view between writes are not expressible; BytesIOWritelines states only the all-succeed case.

name: _io_BytesIO_close_impl
reason: C.step .close mirrors :889-891 (CHECK_EXPORTS, then clear, no CHECK_CLOSED), but its entries never take a view (core is export-free, the twins-agree and no-alloc-fail counterexamples close without one), so a close that dropped the buffer under a live view passes them; BytesIOGetbuffer does pin C close with a view to BufferError for a non-empty stream, so adding _io_BytesIO_close_impl to pyio-bytesio-getbuffer's pyFns would fix this row.

name: bytesio_getstate
reason: C.xstep .getstate is the closed check and (buf, pos, None), so the instance-dict branch of bytesio_getstate_lock_held (:921-930: PyDict_Copy of self->dict, and its NULL return) is not mirrored and a getstate that always returned None for the dict passes pickle-roundtrip and pyio-bytesio-getstate; bytesio_getstate_lock_held (:909-935) itself has no inventory row.

name: bytesio_setstate_lock_held
reason: C.setstate takes a byte list and an int, so the TypeErrors for a non-tuple or short state (:963-968), a non-int position (:986-991) and a non-dict third item (:1004-1010), the dict update/assign (:1011-1019), a non-buffer state[0], and the partial application on a bad position (buffer already replaced, modelled but unstated) are outside BytesIOPickleRoundTrip, which states only the success round trip; a setstate that skipped every validation passes.

name: bytesio_setstate
reason: The wrapper only adds a critical section (:1029-1031) around bytesio_setstate_lock_held, whose validation and dict handling are not modelled (see that row).

name: bytesio_new
reason: C.construct starts from ⟨[], 0, open, 0 exports, shared⟩, which is what :1059-1066 build (fields zeroed by tp_alloc, buf the immortal empty bytes), then runs __init__; BytesIOInitTwins pins that both constructors give bInit and that the twins then agree, so a tp_new that left the object closed fails the no-argument case; the NoMemory path cannot fire for the empty singleton.

name: _io_BytesIO___init___impl
reason: C.reinit/reinitObj mirror :1087-1110 (exports refusal first, reset, exact bytes stored and the stream reopened, otherwise write then pos = 0), but the theorems state only the refusal, the exact-bytes and no-value paths and the int-argument TypeError: the non-exact success path (bytearray/memoryview, :1103-1110) and the closed-stream ValueError of that path are unstated, so an __init__ that forgot `self->pos = 0` passes, and a __buffer__ re-entering during the write is not expressible.

name: bytesio_traverse
reason: no-behaviour applies by the GC policy: Py_VISIT of the type, dict and buf only.

name: bytesio_clear
reason: no-behaviour applies by the tp_clear policy: it only drops the dict and, with no exports, the buffer (:1157-1160).

name: bytesiobuf_getbuffer_lock_held
reason: C.takeView keeps only exports + 1 and the `shared` flag (which changes nothing but a SystemError message), not the unshare-before-export (:1243-1246) or the writable PyBuffer_FillInfo over string_size bytes (:1249-1251); since the view is not data in the model, an export that skipped the unshare and let view writes mutate an escaped bytes object passes release-exports and in-range, and 3.15.2 does exactly that for a uniquely held buffer with a cached hash (gh-160181).

name: bytesiobuf_getbuffer
reason: The slot adds the obsolete view == NULL BufferError (:1259-1263, unreachable from Python) and a critical section around bytesiobuf_getbuffer_lock_held, whose aliasing behaviour is not modelled (see that row).

name: bytesiobuf_releasebuffer
reason: bRelease is exports - 1 (:1277); BytesIOReleaseExports pins that getbuffer then release restores the count for every starting count, with contents and position unchanged, so a release that did nothing or reset the count to 0 fails it.

name: bytesiobuf_traverse
reason: no-behaviour applies by the GC policy: Py_VISIT of the type and the source BytesIO only.

name: bytesiobuf_dealloc
reason: no-behaviour applies by the dealloc policy: it untracks, drops the source reference and frees, calling nothing itself.
